key_insight: Deep generative crystal structure prediction performs well, but most of its apparent success overlaps with template retrieval, indicating strong prototype dependence rather than truly de novo discovery.
engineering_relevance: For computational materials design, this suggests generative CSP models should be evaluated as augmented prototype search tools and not assumed to replace template-based methods.
method: Benchmarked 12 generative CSP models across latent-variable, diffusion, flow-matching, autoregressive, and manifold random-walk families.
Used identical symmetry, structure-matching, and consensus criteria against TCSP 2.0.
Performed a leakage-controlled retraining test by removing stoichiometric prototype families from training data.
evidence_signal: On 180 test structures, template retrieval reached 68.3% top-1 success, while the best generative methods were EquiCSP at 66.4% and Uni-3DAR at 62.9%; on a 46-structure leakage-controlled subset, accuracy dropped by 50–78% after prototype-family removal.
watch_item: High benchmark scores may overstate true novelty, because performance can collapse when training prototypes are withheld and much of the success is retrievable from existing libraries.
paper_title: Deep Generative Crystal Structure Prediction: A Benchmark Study and a Controlled Test of Prototype Dependence
